# Churchill Downs Stakes Advances: Dogwood Winner Conceit Back for Closing Day's $300,000 Chilukki; Vanderbilt Winner Built Stretches Out in $250,000 Cherokee Mile


## Nov 22, 2026


Juddmonte’s Dogwood Stakes (Grade III) winner Conceit will attempt to remain unbeaten over the Churchill Downs main track when she headlines next Sunday’s 41st running of the $300,000 Chilukki (GIII).


The one-mile race for fillies and mares shares Sunday’s closing-day stakes spotlight with the $250,000 Cherokee Mile. First post is 1 p.m. (all times Eastern) with the Chilukki scheduled as Race 11 at 5:54 p.m. and the Cherokee Mile as Race 10 at 5:25 p.m.


Trained by Brad Cox, Conceit began a three-race winning streak with a 10 ¼-length allowance victory going one mile over a sloppy track June 26 at Churchill Downs. The 3-year-old homebred daughter of Not This Time followed with a three-quarter-length victory in the $200,000 Audubon Oaks on Aug. 9 at Ellis Park and earned her first graded stakes victory in the $300,000 Dogwood on Sept. 19 when she rallied past Grade I winner Explora and subsequent Raven Run (GII) winner Movie Night in a three-horse photo finish. Her winning streak ended when she finished fourth behind Movie Night in the $400,000 Raven Run four weeks ago at Keeneland. Tyler Gaffalione will ride Conceit in the Chilukki from post No. 3.


Among Conceit’s chief rivals is Reddam Racing’s Look Forward, who returns to the site of her victory in last year’s $600,000 Eight Belles (GII). Trained by Michael McCarthy, the 4-year-old daughter of Bolt d’Oro defeated Blue Fire by 1 ¼ lengths in the seven-furlong Eight Belles on Kentucky Oaks Day before stretching out to 1 1/8 miles and finishing second to La Cara in the $500,000 Acorn (GI) at Saratoga. Look Forward returned from a 13-month layoff to finish second by three-quarters of a length to Usha in the $300,000 Open Mind on Sept. 12 at Churchill Downs. In her only other start this year, she finished 10th in the $1 million Breeders’ Cup Filly & Mare Sprint (GI) on Oct. 31 at Keeneland. Edgar Morales has the call and will exit post 10.


The field for the Chilukki from the rail out (with jockey and trainer):


Roswell (Luis Saez, Bill Mott)
Anna’s Promise (Walter Rodriguez, Carlos David)
Conceit (Gaffalione, Cox)
Takethemoneyhoney (Eliseo Ruiz, Michael Moore)
Miss Authentic (Manny Esquivel, Anna Meah)
Pronghorn (Jose Ortiz, Steve Asmussen)
Queen’s Martini (Florent Geroux, Ron Moquett)
Just Singing (Junior Alvarado, Kent Sweezey)
Union Mist (Brian Hernandez Jr., Brendan Walsh)
Look Forward (Morales, McCarthy)
Sunday’s Closing Day program will feature mandatory payouts in all multi-race sequences including the Derby City 6 Jackpot. For more information and to purchase tickets, visit www.churchilldowns.com.


VANDERBILT WINNER BUILT STRETCHES OUT IN SUNDAY’S $250,000 CHEROKEE MILE – Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners’ Alfred G. Vanderbilt (Grade II) winner Built will stretch out to a mile in search of his third stakes victory of the year in Sunday’s third running of the $250,000 Cherokee Mile at Churchill Downs.


The one-mile race for 3-year-olds and up shares the closing day stakes spotlight with the $300,000 Chilukki (GIII) for fillies and mares. First post is 1 p.m. (all times Eastern) with the Cherokee Mile scheduled as Race 10 at 5:25 p.m.


Trained by Wayne Catalano, Built has developed into one of the country’s leading sprinters this season by winning four of eight starts. His campaign includes a six-furlong track record of 1:07.96 at Fair Grounds in March, a 2 ½-length victory in the $400,000 Vanderbilt on July 25 at Saratoga and a 1 ½-length win in the $300,000 Louisville Thoroughbred Society on Sept. 12 at Churchill Downs. The 4-year-old son of Hard Spun most recently finished sixth in last month’s $2 million Breeders’ Cup Sprint (GI) at Keeneland. Jockey Luis Saez has the mount and will break from post No. 3.


Among Built’s top rivals is Mike and Kay Kay Ball’s Chief Wallabee, who will seek his first stakes victory after finishing second to Dr. Kapur in last month’s $350,000 Perryville (GIII) at Keeneland. Trained by Hall of Famer Bill Mott, the 3-year-old son of Constitution finished second to Commandment in the $425,000 Fountain of Youth (GII) and third in the $1 million Florida Derby (GI) before running fourth, beaten three lengths by Golden Tempo in the $5 million Kentucky Derby presented by Woodford Reserve (GI). Junior Alvarado rides Chief Wallabee from the rail.


The field for the Cherokee Mile from the rail out (with jockey and trainer):


Chief Wallabee (Alvarado, Mott)
Banishing (Tyler Gaffalione, David Jacobson)
Built (Saez, Catalano)
Hall of Fame (Jose Ortiz, Steve Asmussen)
Steeze (Jaime Torres, Riley Mott)
Stop the Car (Edgar Morales, Brendan Walsh)
Jack’s Promise (Manny Esquivel, Dale Romans)
Gearing Up (Axel Concepcion, Rusty Arnold II)
DOWN THE STRETCH – Sunday’s 10-race card began at 1 p.m. and featured a $67,292 carryover in the 20-cent Derby City 6 Jackpot and $501,758 carryover in the Jackpot 8. … Klein Racing’s homebred Quick Pick earned a career-best 91 Brisnet Speed Rating for his dominant 5 ¾-length victory in Race 7 Saturday, a 1 1/8-mile turf allowance contest. Trainer Will Walden said Quick Pick likely will go to Florida this winter and aim toward a spring campaign in Kentucky.
